scenes.visual: Title card 'Downhill for Free' over a thin grey-and-cream membrane line across the screen, blue dots drifting on both sides. THE WORLD, kept for both films: 16:9, warm cream background, flat cartoon shapes, no molecular structures. COLOUR MAP, same in every scene, both films and the lesson's take-homes: WATER molecules = small BLUE dots; SODIUM ions = ORANGE dots labelled 'Na+'; CHLORIDE ions = GREEN dots labelled 'Cl-'; POTASSIUM ions = PURPLE dots labelled 'K+'; ATP = YELLOW token; OXYGEN = small WHITE dots with a grey outline; DYE = RED dots; MEMBRANE = two rows of GREY round heads with PALE cream tails meeting in the middle; PROTEINS in the membrane = TEAL blocks. A small counter box sits top right in every scene. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: There is water inside a cell and water all around it. So how does water know which way to go? To find out, start with something you can see: a drop of dye.
scenes.visual: A cartoon cell floats in a pale blue sea; blue dots fill inside and outside. A question mark pops above the membrane. Camera pulls back to a glass of still water as one red drop falls in.
scenes.narration: There is water inside a cell and water all around it. So how does water know which way to go? To find out, start with something you can see: a drop of dye.

scenes.tts: Drop dye into still water. Each dye molecule jiggles and bumps at random. Now draw a line down the middle, and count the crossings each way.
scenes.visual: Red dots bunched on the left of a tank, each jittering on a random path. A dashed vertical midline appears. Counter box: 'left to right' and 'right to left' tallies start ticking.
scenes.narration: Drop dye into still water. Each dye molecule jiggles and bumps at random. Now draw a line down the middle, and count the crossings each way.

scenes.tts: At first, far more cross from the crowded side, simply because more are there to cross. Later the dye is even. Crossings still happen, equally both ways. The molecules never stopped moving. There is just no net movement.
scenes.visual: Left-to-right tally races ahead while red dots spread right. Once even, both tallies tick at the same rate. Caption on screen: 'still moving, no net movement'.
scenes.narration: At first, far more cross from the crowded side, simply because more are there to cross. Later the dye is even. Crossings still happen, equally both ways. The molecules never stopped moving. There is just no net movement.

scenes.tts: A difference in concentration from one place to another is a concentration gradient. In open water, with no energy spent, a substance moves on balance down its gradient, from more concentrated to less. That spreading is diffusion.
scenes.visual: A shaded ramp appears under the tank, dark red on the left fading to pale on the right, labelled 'concentration gradient'. A ball rolls down the ramp, labelled 'diffusion: down the gradient, no energy'.
scenes.narration: A difference in concentration from one place to another is a concentration gradient. In open water, with no energy spent, a substance moves on balance down its gradient, from more concentrated to less. That spreading is diffusion.

scenes.tts: Now put a cell membrane in the way. It is two rows of phospholipids, heads facing the water, oily tails tucked inside. Small oxygen molecules slip straight through the oily middle.
scenes.visual: Zoom to a membrane across the screen: grey heads out, pale tails meeting in the middle, labelled 'phospholipid'. White oxygen dots drift through the tail region from top to bottom.
scenes.narration: Now put a cell membrane in the way. It is two rows of phospholipids, heads facing the water, oily tails tucked inside. Small oxygen molecules slip straight through the oily middle.

scenes.tts: Charged ions, such as sodium and chloride, bounce off the oily middle. They cross mainly through proteins. Water crosses too, much of it through protein water channels. A membrane like this is selectively permeable.
scenes.caption: Charged ions, such as sodium (Na+) and chloride (Cl-), bounce off the oily middle. They cross mainly through proteins. Water crosses too, much of it through protein water channels. A membrane like this is selectively permeable.
scenes.visual: Orange Na+ and green Cl- dots bounce off the tails. A teal channel block opens in the membrane; a stream of blue water dots passes through it. Label: 'selectively permeable'.
scenes.narration: Charged ions, such as sodium (Na+) and chloride (Cl-), bounce off the oily middle. They cross mainly through proteins. Water crosses too, much of it through protein water channels. A membrane like this is selectively permeable.

scenes.tts: Now join two tanks with this membrane. Both hold pure water, at the same level. Water crosses both ways, equally. Then stir salt into the left tank only. The salt cannot cross.
scenes.visual: Two side-by-side tanks of blue water separated by the membrane, levels equal. Counter: water crossings per second, left to right and right to left, equal. A spoon tips orange and green dots into the left tank; they bounce off the membrane and stay left.
scenes.narration: Now join two tanks with this membrane. Both hold pure water, at the same level. Water crosses both ways, equally. Then stir salt into the left tank only. The salt cannot cross.

scenes.tts: Water can cross. Salt cannot. Which tank's water level will rise, the salty one or the pure one? Pause the film and decide.
scenes.visual: Pause card 'Pause and predict' over the two tanks. Two arrows hover above the tanks with question marks: 'left rises?' and 'right rises?'
scenes.narration: Water can cross. Salt cannot. Which tank's water level will rise, the salty one or the pure one? Pause the film and decide.

scenes.tts: The left tank rises, the salty side. Look closely at one drop from each side. On the left, some particles in each drop are salt, not water. So each drop holds fewer water molecules.
scenes.visual: Left level climbs, right level drops. Two magnified circles: right drop full of blue dots; left drop where some of the places are taken by orange and green dots, so it holds fewer blue dots. Label: 'fewer water molecules per drop' (schematic).
scenes.narration: The left tank rises, the salty side. Look closely at one drop from each side. On the left, some particles in each drop are salt, not water. So each drop holds fewer water molecules.

scenes.tts: So more water molecules reach the membrane from the right each second, and more cross to the left. Water is running down its own gradient. That net movement of water is osmosis.
scenes.visual: Counter: right-to-left crossings now outpace left-to-right. A blue ramp appears pointing from the pure side down toward the salty side, labelled 'water's own gradient'. Label: 'osmosis'.
scenes.narration: So more water molecules reach the membrane from the right each second, and more cross to the left. Water is running down its own gradient. That net movement of water is osmosis.

scenes.tts: Does the left tank rise forever? No. The taller column of water presses back on the membrane. The rise stops when that push balances the difference in water.
scenes.visual: Left column now taller; a downward arrow labelled 'push of the taller column' grows until the crossing counters equal again. Level freezes. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Does the left tank rise forever? No. The taller column of water presses back on the membrane. The rise stops when that push balances the difference in water.

scenes.tts: Nothing in this film spent any energy. Dye, oxygen and water all ran downhill on their own. The salt never crossed at all. Moving anything uphill would cost energy, and that is the second film's story.
scenes.visual: Recap strip: red dye spreading, white oxygen slipping through, blue water crossing toward salt, each with a downhill ramp icon and a crossed-out yellow ATP token labelled 'no energy spent'; orange and green salt dots bounce off the membrane, labelled 'cannot cross'. An uphill ramp appears greyed out with a yellow token and a question mark.
scenes.narration: Nothing in this film spent any energy. Dye, oxygen and water all ran downhill on their own. The salt never crossed at all. Moving anything uphill would cost energy, and that is the second film's story.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule. With no energy spent, whatever can cross runs down its own gradient. And water runs toward the dissolved particles that cannot cross.
scenes.visual: The two tanks return, and the rule types out on screen one phrase at a time as the narrator speaks.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule. With no energy spent, whatever can cross runs down its own gradient. And water runs toward the dissolved particles that cannot cross.

scenes.visual: End card, Hex mascot beside the line: 'Whatever can cross runs downhill for free; water runs toward trapped solute.'
